note: All figures are transcribed from SSC's official result write-ups (ssc.gov.in / ssc.nic.in; ssc.nic.in files are also linked via the Internet Archive because that host is often unreachable). Tier-I is out of 200 marks in every year listed. Cut-offs are the marks of the last candidate shortlisted in each category for the next stage, not pass marks. From CGL 2018 onward Tier-I (and multi-shift Tier-II) marks are normalised scores (SSC formula of 07.02.2019; from CGL 2025 the revised methodology of 02.06.2025), which is why they have 5 decimals; 40.00000 or similar round values are usually the statutory minimum (30% UR, 25% OBC/EWS, 20% others; e.g. 40/200 = 20%). CGL 2017 write-up gives unnormalised-looking values. SSC fixes separate cut-offs per post group (e.g. AAO, JSO, Statistical Investigator Gr. II, all other posts); group labels follow each year's write-up. UR cut-off can be lower than a reserved category's because reserved candidates meeting the UR standard are counted as UR-qualified. Up to CGL 2021 final merit = Tier-I + Tier-II + Tier-III (out of 700 for general posts), and the Tier-II stage cut-off is on Tier-I + Tier-II; from CGL 2022 Tier-I is qualifying only and merit is on Tier-II alone (Paper-I Sections I+II = 390; +Paper-II Statistics 200 for JSO/SI). Category keys: UR, OBC, EWS (from 2019), SC, ST, ESM (ex-servicemen), OH (orthopedically handicapped), HH (hearing), VH (visually), PwD-Others. A missing category means no vacancy/no list for it that year, never zero.
